hints: Notice each pulse is $1.0\text{ m}$ long at $t=0$, from $4.0$ to $5.0\text{ m}$ and from $7.0$ to $8.0\text{ m}$, with speed $0.50\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the centre.
Calculate how far each leading edge moves in $3.0\text{ s}$ using $s = vt$, then find the new position interval for each pulse.
Compare the up and down displacements where the two pulses overlap and recall that resultant displacement is the vector sum of the two separate displacements.
walkthrough: Find the distance travelled in $3.0\text{ s}$: $s = vt = 0.50 \times 3.0 = 1.5\text{ m}$.

Move the left pulse $1.5\text{ m}$ to the right: $4.0$ to $5.0\text{ m}$ becomes $5.5$ to $6.5\text{ m}$. Move the right pulse $1.5\text{ m}$ to the left: $7.0$ to $8.0\text{ m}$ becomes $5.5$ to $6.5\text{ m}$.
The two $1.0\text{ m}$ pulses therefore lie exactly on top of each other between $5.5$ and $6.5\text{ m}$ at $t = 3.0\text{ s}$.
At $t=0$ both pulses have the same shape and polarity, crest over crest and trough over trough, so where they overlap the principle of superposition gives $y = y_1 + y_2$ with the same sign.
Identical displacements add to double amplitude, while the rope outside $5.5$ to $6.5\text{ m}$ has zero displacement from both pulses.
Only the diagram with a double-height wave confined between $5.5$ and $6.5\text{ m}$ matches this. This is option C

A.explanation: Shows four normal-amplitude waves spread from 5.0 to 7.0 m, which would be the two pulses placed end to end without overlapping and without adding displacements.

B.explanation: Shows unequal peaks with one very large central peak, which does not follow from adding two identical $1.0\text{ m}$ long pulses exactly on top of each other.

C.explanation: Shows a $1.0\text{ m}$ long wave of double amplitude centred at 6.0 m, which is the result of the two identical in-phase pulses fully overlapping and adding.

D.explanation: Shows a flat rope, which would require complete cancellation by an inverted pulse, but both pulses in the $t=0$ diagram have displacements in the same direction.
